pll1d33c2-d1e3501.summary: Asks how the properties, which cannot be in the persons without determining them, can be in the divine essence without determining it.

pll1d33c2-d1e3504.summary: Answers with Hilary: I do not know, I do not inquire, yet I will console myself; archangels, angels, prophets, and apostles do not know, and the Son did not reveal it. Let no one think he can grasp the mystery of generation. The meaning stops here: the Son is from the Father, only-begotten from unbegotten, living from living, one nature. Begin, persevere; though you will not arrive, you will progress, but do not presume to comprehend.
claims: The mystery of generation exceeds human understanding.
Pious inquiry progresses though it cannot comprehend.

pll1d33c2-d1e3537.summary: Concludes from this and many texts that we may not scrutinize majesty, set law to power, or circumscribe the infinite.
claims: We may not scrutinize the divine majesty.

pll1d33c2-d1e3550.summary: Reports the opponents citing Augustine on Ps 68: God is substance; what the Father is as God, the Son and Spirit are; but when he is Father, he is not that which he is, since 'Father' is said relative to the Son, not 'ad se.' So the Son is said to be God but not Father.
claims: What the Father is as God is substance.

pll1d33c2-d1e3582.summary: Gives their interpretation: Augustine shows that what makes God is substance, but what makes the Father is not substance; so the Father's property is not the essence.

pll1d33c2-d1e3585.summary: Gives Lombard's interpretation: Augustine means that by what he is God he is substance, but he is not Father by that by which he is substance, since he is Father by the property of generation. He did not deny that the property is substance. Likewise 'when he is Father, he is not what he is' means he is Father not by essence but by notion.
claims: The Father is Father by notion, not by essence.
Augustine did not deny that the property is substance.

pll1d33c2-d1e3590.summary: Reports another argument from Augustine's 'the Word, as wisdom and essence, is what the Father is; as Word, not': so the property by which he is Word is not what the Father is, not the divine essence.

pll1d33c2-d1e3596.summary: Answers that although the Word as Word is not what the Father is, the property by which he is Word is what the Father is, the divine essence, but not the Father's hypostasis.
claims: The property of the Word is the divine essence, but not the Father's hypostasis.

pl-l1d33c2.summary: Asks how the properties can be in the essence without determining it, when they cannot be in the persons without determining them. Lombard answers with Hilary: I do not know, I do not inquire; angels and prophets did not know, the Son did not reveal it; the mystery of generation cannot be grasped by human intellect, so one should advance piously but not presume to comprehend. The opponents cite Augustine on Psalm 68 ('what the Father is, is not of substance') to show the Father's property is not God; Lombard reads it as meaning that the Father is not Father by that by which he is substance, without denying that the property is substance. Likewise 'the Word, as Word, is not what the Father is' means the property is the divine essence but not the Father's hypostasis.
claims: How the properties are in the essence without determining it cannot be comprehended.
The mystery of generation exceeds human understanding; one may progress but not comprehend.
The Father is not Father by that by which he is substance, yet his property is substance.
The property by which the Word is Word is the divine essence, but not the Father's hypostasis.
